discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies by WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model and quantitative tests of the primordial fluctuations
motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe changed cosmology from an order-of-magnitude subject into a precision science. Bennett (Principal Investigator), Page (instrument and calibration) and Spergel (analysis and theory) led a mission whose full-sky, carefully controlled maps of temperature and polarization anisotropies fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe to percent accuracy. WMAP showed that the universe is spatially flat and dominated by dark energy and non-baryonic dark matter. It measured the baryon density independently of nucleosynthesis and detected early reionization through large-angle polarization. It also found that the primordial fluctuations are adiabatic, nearly Gaussian and slightly tilted away from scale invariance (n_s < 1), which made the physics of the earliest moments empirically testable. Its rigorous treatment of systematics and its open data release set the template for Planck and every later survey. This is a discovery-level achievement in fundamental physics.
